title: Telemonitoring for outpatient follow-up care of patients with non-invasive ventilation at home
summary:
Previous research on the home-based care of patients receiving non-invasive ventilation (NIV) is still quite limited. A prior study conducted by the responsible research group developed and tested a specific care algorithm designed to provide structured outpatient management for this patient population. The results showed that it is indeed feasible to monitor NIV therapy outside the hospital setting. In addition, the study established a decision-making model that can help determine whether inpatient treatment is necessary.

The current study investigates whether non-invasive ventilation can be reliably monitored at home using modern telemedicine. Ventilation data are recorded in the home setting and transmitted digitally to the medical team. The goal is to determine whether this form of care is practical and effective in everyday life. At the same time, the study aims to evaluate whether telemedicine-supported care can improve both the quality of ventilation and the patients' quality of life.
conditions: Chronic respiratory insufficiency, not elsewhere classified: Type II [hypercapnic]

interventions.name:
•Mobile arterial blood gas analysis (ABG): Outpatient measurement of pH, pCO₂, pO₂, HCO₃⁻, and other parameters to assess the respiratory status.
•Telemonitoring (recording of ventilation parameters and usage times)
•Transcutaneous CO₂ monitoring using the Sentec system: Non-invasive, continuous C

The comparison of study outcomes is based on a historical control group. This group consists of patients from the previous cohort of the inpatient population of the OCONIV study, in which care was provided in accordance with the current clinical guideline in an inpatient setting. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with established non-invasive ventilation (NIV) therapy for at least three months due to type 2 respiratory failure

Presence of capacity to consent as well as signed data protection and informed consent documents
Exclusion criteria:
Age under 18 years

Presence of deafness

Lack of capacity to consent without legal guardianship
